column2: a cozy two-storey half-timbered townhouse: cream plaster walls with dark brown timber framing, a steep terracotta tile gable roof with a slight overhang, one brick chimney, the upper floor slightly jutting out over the ground floor, a wooden front door with a small step and a lantern beside it, small-paned windows with green shutters and a flower box with red flowers. Compact footprint about 6 m wide and 5 m deep, about 8 m tall to the roof ridge.

a village stone well: round wall of rough grey fieldstones about 1.6 m wide and 0.8 m high, two thick wooden posts holding a small pitched wooden shingle roof, a wooden crank with rope and a bucket hanging in the middle, a little moss on the stones.

a medieval market stall: a wooden counter table about 2.5 m wide with crates of apples, pears and vegetables on top and baskets in front, four wooden posts holding a red-and-cream striped cloth canopy that slopes forward, a small hanging wooden sign.

a narrow tall three-storey medieval townhouse: pale blue-grey plaster walls with dark timber framing, each upper floor jutting out a little over the one below, a very steep slate-blue tile gable roof, a small dormer window, tall small-paned windows with white frames and blue shutters, a narrow arched wooden front door with a lantern. Footprint about 5 m wide and 5 m deep, about 11 m tall.

a wide one-storey cozy cottage: lower walls of rounded grey fieldstone, upper gable of cream plaster with timber, a thick rounded terracotta tile roof with a little moss, a round attic window, a chunky wooden door with a little porch roof, flower boxes with yellow flowers, a stone chimney on one end. Footprint about 8 m wide and 5.5 m deep, about 6 m tall.

a two-storey village bakery: warm yellow plaster walls with brown timber framing, a big shop window on the ground floor with loaves of bread visible and a striped green-and-white fabric awning above it, a hanging wooden sign shaped like a loaf of bread, an orange tile gable roof, a large brick oven chimney. Footprint about 7 m wide and 6 m deep, about 9 m tall.

a large three-storey medieval tavern inn: dark timber framing over white plaster, a stone ground floor with a wide double wooden door, a wooden balcony on the second floor with flower pots, a hanging sign with a golden tankard, a big red tile roof with two dormer windows and two chimneys. Footprint about 8 m wide and 6 m deep, about 12 m tall.

a blacksmith's workshop house: thick stone ground floor with a wide open-front forge alcove containing an anvil and a glowing hearth (shallow alcove, not a hole through), timber-framed upper floor with brown plaster, a dark grey slate roof, a tall soot-stained stone chimney, a hanging sign with a horseshoe, a barrel of water and tools by the door. Footprint about 7 m wide and 5.5 m deep, about 9 m tall.

a two-storey townhouse with soft pink plaster walls and white window trims, a hipped (four-sided) brown-red tile roof with a small dormer, green shutters, window boxes full of lavender, a teal wooden front door with a small round window, a bench beside the door. Footprint about 6 m wide and 6 m deep, about 9 m tall.

a corner townhouse with a small round turret on one front corner: cream and light-green plaster walls with timber framing, the turret has a pointed green cone roof, the main roof is a green tile gable roof, a wooden front door with a lantern, small-paned windows with red shutters. Footprint about 7 m wide and 6 m deep, about 11 m tall.

a medieval market stall selling pottery and cloth: a wooden counter about 2.5 m wide with stacked clay pots, jugs and folded colourful fabrics, four wooden posts holding a blue-and-white striped cloth canopy that slopes forward, a hanging wooden sign.

a medieval market stall selling flowers and honey: a wooden counter about 2.5 m wide with buckets of colourful flower bouquets and jars of honey, four wooden posts holding a yellow-and-white striped cloth canopy that slopes forward, a hanging wooden sign shaped like a flower.

a round town-square stone fountain: a wide low circular basin of carved pale stone about 6 m across filled with blue water, a central pedestal with a smaller upper bowl spilling water, a little stone fish statue on top, a few lily pads, small moss in the joints.

a round medieval castle wall tower: thick cylindrical tower of warm beige-grey stone blocks about 7 m in diameter and 11 m tall, a crenellated top with a slight overhang ring, a tall pointed slate-blue cone roof on top, a few narrow arrow-slit windows, a small banner on the roof tip. Total height about 17 m.

a medieval castle gatehouse: two square stone towers about 4 m wide joined by a wall with a large wide-open arched gateway in the middle about 6 m wide and 5 m tall that passes straight through the building (you can see through it), a raised iron portcullis at the top of the arch, crenellations, hipped slate-blue roofs on both towers, a coat-of-arms shield above the arch. About 15 m wide, 6 m deep and 15 m tall.

a fairy-tale castle keep: a big square stone hall with tall arched windows on a stone plinth, four round corner towers with tall pointed slate-blue cone roofs, a taller central spire with a flag, a grand arched wooden main door with stairs in front, banners hanging on the walls. About 20 m wide, 18 m deep and 33 m tall.
a cluster of market goods: three wooden barrels with iron bands, two stacked wooden crates with apples and cabbages, a burlap sack leaning against them. About 2 m wide.
a wooden farm hand-cart with two big spoked wheels and two handles, loaded with hay bales and a few pumpkins. About 3 m long.
a cozy medieval street lamp post: a dark wrought-iron post on a small stone base, with a curled arm holding a glass lantern with a warm candle inside. About 3.5 m tall.
a wooden park bench with a backrest, sturdy wooden legs and iron details, a small potted flower next to it on the ground. About 2 m long.
a neat stack of chopped firewood logs under a tiny wooden lean-to roof, an axe stuck in a chopping stump next to it. About 2 m wide.

a straight modular section of a medieval castle curtain wall, made to be tiled end to end: warm beige-grey stone block masonry (same stone as a round castle tower), about 10 m long, 7 m tall and 2.5 m thick, a row of chunky crenellations (merlons) along the top on both edges, a slightly wider stone plinth at the bottom, a few patches of moss and ivy at the base, both long faces similar. The two short ends are FLAT vertical cuts showing the wall cross-section so sections can join seamlessly. The FRONT view shows the long outer face.

a short straight modular section of a medieval castle curtain wall, made to be tiled end to end: warm beige-grey stone block masonry, about 5 m long, 6 m tall and 2.5 m thick (roughly as tall as it is long), with exactly 3 big chunky square merlons (crenellations) on top with deep wide gaps between them, the merlons clearly separated and as thick as the wall, a slightly wider stone plinth at the bottom, a little moss and ivy at the base, both long faces similar. The two short ends are FLAT vertical cuts showing the wall cross-section so sections can join seamlessly. The FRONT view shows the long outer face.
